audit.whatIsWrong: The full layer gave Lucian rows 0-3 and 'Skill' for 4-6 while the content layer gave him 0-3 and 'Skill' for 4-6 too — both disagreeing with the packet chart (Lucian, Skill, Lillia, Lillia, Lillia, Lillia, Lillia) and with the mirror, which already committed to that chart. The header also read EVEN 5.5/10 while the mirror set its side to FAV 4/10.
audit.why: The page's own whys[2..6] all describe Lillia owning those stages — E bouncing off the wave to break the dash, W move speed out-kiting a 500-range marksman, the R sleep interrupting The Culling. Only the side tokens disagreed with the prose.
audit.corrected: Rows 1-6 set to Skill, Lillia, Lillia, Lillia, Lillia, Lillia in both layers as matched pairs, ratings re-scaled to 5/4/3/3/3/2, and the header restated as a tricky 7/10 matchup with the orange tone so it matches the mirror's inverse.

audit.whatIsWrong: phases[4] described level 6 as Lucian's own ult spike; on this lane 6 is Lillia's. No cooldown appeared anywhere on the chart.
audit.why: Lilting Lullaby is 150/130/110s at 1600 range and puts everyone carrying Dream Dust to sleep — it interrupts The Culling's channel outright, which is the decisive level-6 fact.
audit.corrected: phases[4].why now names Lilting Lullaby and its 150s rank-1 cooldown with the do-not-channel rule; Swirlseed's flat 12s added to the Do's and Don'ts.

audit.whatIsWrong: The packet flags that this matchup never names a single Lillia ability, and the resistances-invalidated interaction was absent entirely.
audit.why: Blooming Blows (Q) is a 450-range ring on 6/5.5/5/4.5/4s whose outer edge deals extra TRUE damage — buying armour or MR misprices every trade. Swirlseed (E) is 700 range on a flat 12s and keeps rolling until it hits a wall, which is why it catches you after you think you dodged it.
audit.corrected: Blooming Blows' range, cooldown and true-damage edge written into report[5].t; Swirlseed's roll-to-wall behaviour and 12s cooldown into dontsFull[0].d and dosFull[2].d; Lilting Lullaby into phases[4].why.

edits.before: E online — dash-weave trades start now: spell, double-shot, dash out before his answer lands.
edits.after: Both spike at 2, but her W kite and E bounce make a clean all-in a coinflip, not a free kill.

edits.before: Full kit: Q-AA-E-AA-W-AA strings chunk a third of his HP. Trade on every CS he takes from the wrong angle.
edits.after: Her E bounces off the wave to break your dash, and W move speed means your 500 range never pins her.

edits.before: Keep the pressure rolling but track Blooming Blows — your lead is HP-bar bullying, not all-in math, until items arrive.
edits.after: Her passive burn plus W-E kiting makes every Q step-up cost you more sustained damage than it costs her.

edits.before: The Culling adds lane-clear and execute chip — use it through walls on recalls and low-HP escapes.
edits.after: Lilting Lullaby sleeps you mid-Culling on a 150s cooldown — never channel R with her ult up.

edits.before: First item spike is your kill window — the dash-weave combo now deletes half bars. Force the issue before he stabilizes.
edits.after: Her first AP item perma-pokes and kites; your first-item spike cannot catch a champion this slippery.

edits.before: You fall off relative to top-lane scalers — convert the lead into towers and roams before the 3-item brawlers arrive.
edits.after: She out-scales you hard — burn damage plus W move speed kite you down and a weak scaler has no answer.

edits.before: Track Lillia’s Blooming Blows: Her kiting speed stacks — catch her early in the chase or not at all. The whole green-light system is its cooldown.
edits.after: Blooming Blows is a 450 ring on 6s and its outer edge deals true damage, so armour will not price the trade. Catch her before the speed stacks.

edits.before: Lillia whiffs Blooming Blows and the lane briefly belongs to you.
edits.after: Lillia whiffs Swirlseed — a flat 12s with no disengage left.

edits.before: That is Lillia’s rehearsed moment — don’t audition for it.
edits.after: Swirlseed rolls on until it hits a wall — 700 range, flat 12s.

notes: Confidence on the header change (EVEN 5.5/10 to TRICKY 7/10) is Medium, and the mirror flagged the same call on its own side as Medium for the same reason: it rests on the packet chart, this page's own prose, and a 50% win rate over just 12 recorded games, not on a mechanical fact. I made it anyway because leaving diff=EVEN next to a chart where Lillia owns five of seven rows would ship a page that argues with itself. If the user wants the header held at EVEN, the chart is the part backed by the packet and should stay.
